title: Recursive shelves: Positive-ink invoice
topics: Recursion, sorting, binary search and bits
summary: Divide-and-conquer recursion. Add the positive numbers.
descriptionMd:
Inputs
`readings` is a list of integers (numbers with no decimal part). It may be empty, and numbers may repeat unless task 1 says otherwise.

Your tasks
1. Create a list `sectionSums`. Start with the whole `readings` list as a section. Record the sum of that section. If it has more than one number, split it into a left half and a right half. Use the same steps on the left half first, then on the right half. When a section has an odd length, the left half has one fewer number. A section with one number is not split. Do not record empty sections. `sectionSums` contains the sums in the order you record them.
2. Add only the numbers in `sectionSums` that are greater than 0. Store the sum in `positiveTotal`.
3. Complete `recursiveShelvesPositiveInkInvoice` so it returns `positiveTotal`. Return it, do not print it.

Example
If `readings` is [2, 2, 4, -1, 2], then `sectionSums` is [9, 4, 2, 2, 5, 4, 1, -1, 2] and `recursiveShelvesPositiveInkInvoice` returns 29.

Rules
- Skip 0 and negative numbers.
- If no number is greater than 0, return 0.

Test data
TEST DATA 1: `readings` is [-7, 6, 9, 6, 0].
TEST DATA 2: `readings` is [9, -9, 9, 9].

constraints: Answers fit in a signed 32-bit integer: -2,147,483,648 through 2,147,483,647.
Input numbers have no decimal part. They range from -1,000,000 to 1,000,000. Follow any extra input rules in task 1.
Efficiency goal: time O(n log n); extra memory, including the helper list, O(n). n is the input length. These labels describe how work and memory grow with the input.

`sectionSums` is [18, 0, 9, -9, 18, 9, 9]. Keep [18, 9, 18, 9, 9] and add those numbers. Return 63.
`sectionSums` is []. Keep [] and add those numbers. Return 0.
